ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Possible salicylate toxicity

An adult repeatedly exceeds the labeled bismuth subsalicylate dose for diarrhea and develops ringing in the ears. He asks whether to keep increasing the dose because diarrhea persists. Which response is most appropriate?

  1. Add aspirin to improve the same mechanism
  2. Assume tinnitus confirms successful eradication of H. pylori
  3. Continue indefinitely without reviewing hydration
  4. Stop the product and seek medical advice about possible toxicity
  5. Increase the dose until the tinnitus stops
Answer and explanation

Stop the product and seek medical advice about possible toxicity

Tinnitus during excessive salicylate exposure is a warning sign; persistent diarrhea also needs reassessment.

Option explanations

Stop the product and seek medical advice about possible toxicity: Tinnitus during excessive salicylate exposure is a warning sign; persistent diarrhea also needs reassessment.

Increase the dose until the tinnitus stops: Further exposure can worsen toxicity.

Add aspirin to improve the same mechanism: This adds salicylate exposure.

Assume tinnitus confirms successful eradication of H. pylori: Tinnitus is not a marker of eradication.

Continue indefinitely without reviewing hydration: Persistent diarrhea and overuse require assessment.
